blocks.content: You've found the data you want to alert on. Now, open the alert rule creation GUI and give the rule a descriptive name.
To create a new alert rule, complete the following steps:
In the left-hand navigation menu, click **Alerting** under **Alerts & IRM**.
Click **Alert rules** to open the Alert rules page.
Click **+ New alert rule** in the top right. The alert rule creation GUI opens with six numbered sections.

In section 1, **Enter alert rule name**, type a descriptive name that tells you what condition is being monitored.

| Good name | Why it works |
|-----------|--------------|
| High CPU on production servers | Specific about what and where |
| Error rate spike, API gateway | Clear about the signal and the service |

| Avoid | Why |
|-------|-----|
| Alert 1 | Impossible to route or troubleshoot later |
| CPU alert | Too vague when you have dozens of rules |
Your alert rule is named. Next, you'll learn why the name you choose matters more than you might expect.
